articleTitle: A Fully Integrated 0.48 THz FMCW Radar Transceiver MMIC in a SiGe-Technology
abstract: Radar systems are gaining in popularity and spreading into more and more applications due to their robust measurement method. While single-chip solutions have been published in the last decade in the upper millimetre-wave range, solutions are still very limited in the lower THz range. In this paper, a 0.48 THz FMCW-radar transceiver MMIC in a 130 nm silicon-germanium (SiGe) technology is presented. The MMIC consists of one Tx and Rx channel, respectively. The components for frequency synthesis and on-chip patch antennas are fully integrated into the MMIC. The achievable tuning range of the MMIC is 0.448 - 0.491 THz with a peak on-chip output power of about -9.4 dBm. The MMIC was designed and manufactured with the IHP SG13G3 technoloay,

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Low-Noise SiGe HBT Distributed Amplifier with 13 dBm Output Power and 20 dB Gain in D-Band and over 170 GHz Bandwidth
abstract: This paper presents a single-stage distributed amplifier with an average gain of 19 dB and over 170 GHz bandwidth (measurement limited) resulting in > 1.5 THz gain-bandwidth product (GBW). The amplifier is composed of 10 gain sections using an emitter follower buffered cascode stage and is implemented in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS process with 470 GHz f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/ 650 GHz f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>HBT. The amplifier has over 14 dBm saturated output power (Psat) in W-Band and averages 13 dBm Psat with 20 dB gain in D-Band. Additionally, an average noise figure of 4.7 dB was measured over the complete 75 - 110 GHz range. This amplifier has, to the author's knowledge, the highest single-stage GBW reported to date while at the same time providing high output power and the best reported wideband noise figure for SiGe BiCMOS amplifiers in W-Band.

articleTitle: A 23.5-dBm, 7.9%-PAE Pseudo-differential Power Amplifier at 136 GHz in 40-nm GaN
abstract: A pseudo-differential power amplifier (PA) is demonstrated at 136-GHz in a 40-nm GaN HEMT technology. The 2-stage design achieves an output power of 23.5 dBm and peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 7.9% with an associated gain of 7.6 dB. To improve the overall gain in this frequency band, the design incorporates HEMT cells with 3-via inductive source degeneration for gain peaking and improved compression. Pseudo-differential power combining is also implemented using on-chip Marchand baluns with common-source devices. The PA area is 1.26 x 1.13 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mm^{2}$</tex>. To the author's knowledge, this compact PA demonstrates the highest power added efficiency (PAE) in GaN above 135 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency D-Band Frequency Doubler in 22-nm FDSOI CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a high-efficiency D-band push-push frequency doubler implemented in 22-nm FDSOI CMOS technology. A 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic load-pull approach is followed, and a maximum output power of 4.1 dBm is achieved at 135 GHz while the circuit consumes only 24.7 mW from a 800 mV supply. The conversion gain peaks at -3.8 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth of 125–145 GHz (14.9%). The measured peak DC-to-RF efficiency and total efficiency values are 11.8 % and 9.1% respectively, which presents to the authors' best knowledge a leading-edge performance among the reported active CMOS frequency doublers at this frequency range.

articleTitle: A Fully Differential Hybrid Coupler for Automotive Radar Applications
abstract: In this paper, a fully differential hybrid coupler manufactured in a 130 nm SiGe technology is proposed. The designed coupler offers a phase error below 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> and an amplitude imbalance below 2 dB in the bandwidth of interest between 70 GHz and 90 GHz. Furthermore, a method to characterize the proposed coupler with a four-port vector network analyzer is presented. In addition, a transmitter circuit containing a quadrature modulator using the proposed coupler has been designed. Thereby an image suppression ratio of more than 30 dB has been achieved.

articleTitle: A Simple Thermally Activated Trapping Model for AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
abstract: AlGaN/GaN HEMTs have become the technology of choice for RF power amplification, thus exacerbating the importance of accurate circuital models for them. As known, these devices suffer from significant electron trapping effects, which strongly impact their behavior, making a trapping model critical to correctly predict the HEMT response. Physically, it is well known that electron trapping is thermally activated, and, consequently, the device's thermal response interacts with the trapping dynamics. In this paper, we propose a simple circuital trapping model that incorporates the thermal dependency, along with the required characterization techniques for its correct extraction, and show the importance of the trapping thermal dependency inclusion in the prediction of device behavior.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Voltage D-band LNA in 22 nm FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents a low voltage D-band Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) manufactured in a 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator FDSOI CMOS technology. The circuit consists of 4 differential stages. The first stage is optimized for minimal noise, while the other three are optimized to achieve maximum gain. Therefore, a capacitive neutralization technique is applied. Transmission-line-based matching networks are used to match the stages for a bandwidth of over 20 GHz. The measurement results show a gain of 17 dB while achieving a low noise figure of less than 8 dB at a supply voltage of only 0.8 V.

articleTitle: A 67 GHz 23 mW Receiver Utilizing Complementary Current Reuse Techniques
abstract: This paper presents a very low power, low noise receiver operating at V-band which is enabled by the application of ultra-low power RF design techniques in the mmWave domain. This device takes advantage of both complementary current reuse and moderate inversion biasing, combined with a compact and extremely power efficient frequency doubler, to acheive 23 mW power consumption while operating between 60 GHz and 75 GHz for an RF bandwidth of 15 GHz. The receiver achieves superior noise performance compared to other receivers operating at similar power in the same band, enabling a state-of-the-art power versus noise performance. The receiver achieves 3.6 dB of NF, -21.5 dB PldB and 15 GHz BW while consuming only 23 mW. The obtained power consumption normalized to its noise figure shows a significant improvement over existing art, making it an ideal candidate for integration into digital beamforming arrays where low power and low noise are desirable to optimize effective isotropic sensitivity under a given power constraint.

articleTitle: Localization of Trapping Effects in GaN HEMTs with Pulsed S-parameters and Compact Models
abstract: Reliable operation at high frequencies has established GaN-based electronics in the high-power and high-frequency market. Investigating the impact of trapping effects on the frequency evolution of GaN HEMTs is a crucial field for technology optimization. In this paper, we compare devices operating at different frequencies to localize the main source of trapping and a possible connection to HEMT scaling. Pulsed S-parameter and load-pull measurements, analyzed by a small- and a large-signal model, signify the great importance of passivation layers for trap-induced parasitic effects.

articleTitle: 150 GBd PAM-4 Electrical Signal Generation using SiGe-Based Analog Multiplexer Ic
abstract: We present a 2:1 analog multiplexer evaluation board for increasing the analog bandwidth of digital-to-analog converters, based on an integrated circuit in IHP's new 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology generation SG13G3. The resulting significant leap in performance of the IC with a signal path 3-dB-bandwidth of more than 110 GHz is used to generate ultra-high bandwidth 4-level pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM) signals at 150 GBd and 120 GBd, as well as 8-level PAM signals at 120 GBd, utilizing advanced digital signal processing.

articleTitle: An 8 bit 1.73mW 1.25 GS/s Single-Core SAR ADC in 22 nm FDSOI CMOS
abstract: A low-power 8 bit single-core successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with a sampling rate of up to 1.25 GS/s based on alternating comparators is studied. To prove the concept, the circuit is implemented in a 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) technology. Key power dissipating factors are explored considering the high sampling rate. A scheme is investigated, where each memory cell activates the second next memory cell to relax the speed requirement and allow for power savings compared to conventional approaches. A modified, non-overlapped signaling is used in the driver for the capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CDAC) to reduce a direct-path current and to ease the reference buffer design. Measurements show an effective number of bits (ENOB) of 6.86 bit near the Nyquist frequency. A power consumption of 1.73mW is measured, leading to the best Walden figure-of-merit of 11.9 fJ/c.-step for a single-core SAR ADC above 1 GS/s.

articleTitle: Design of two Low DC-Power High-Efficiency D-Band Power Amplifiers in 22 nm FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents two low DC-power D-band power amplifiers (PAs) integrated into a 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) technology. Both amplifiers use the capacitive neutralization technique for gain-boosting and stability enhancement. The design procedure for transformer-based (TB) and line-based (LB) matching networks and the advantages and disadvantages of both architectures are discussed. The PA implementation focuses on low DC-power consumption, high efficiency, and compact device realization. The fabricated TB-and LB-PA show high maximum power-added-efficiency (PAE) of 9 and 8 % consuming 46 and 52mW respectively at a supply voltage of only 0.8 V. The saturated output powers P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> reach 6.8 dBm and 6.5 dBm while achieving small-signal gains of 24.2 and 23.4 dB with 3-dB-bandwidths of 23 and 26 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband 8 W Ka-band MMIC Power Amplifier Using 100 nm GaN Technology
abstract: The downsizing of the gate length in Gallium Nitride (GaN) process allows to target higher frequency application and simultaneously to improve general performances of MMIC with longer gate length. In this paper, we present the first MMIC results achieved on in house GaN based technology under development with 100nm gate length. The Ka-band HPA designed using preliminary design kit elements exhibits an output power greater than 8 W over 26–35 GHz band with a minimum of Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of 26.5 % at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{DD}=15$</tex> V. The compact 11.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> 3-stage HPA has linear gain higher than 23 dB. This demonstrator achieves among the best performances in term of trade-off between output power, gain, PAE and bandwidth. Therefore, this paper is a valuable contribution to the state of the art.

articleTitle: A 30–97 GHz $\mathbf{P}_{\text{sat},3\text{dB}}$ Broadband PA with 18.5-21.5dBm $\mathbf{P}_{\text{sat}}$ and 18-26% PAE in 90nm SiGe Supporting Concurrent Multi-Band Operation
abstract: With the evolving spectral allocations across bands ranging between 24–100 GHz, future mmWave front-ends will need to address multiple band allowing spectral agility and spectrum sharing capabilities for high capacity and robust links. Such characteristics are extremely challenging to achieve in transmitter front-ends particularly at the power amplifiers. This paper presents a broadband and efficient mmWave PA with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{P}_{\text{sat},3\text{dB}}$</tex> bandwidth covering 30–97 GHz capable of supporting concurrent multi-band modulation operation. Implemented in GlobalFoundries 90 nm SiGe process, we employ common-base HBT transistors with broadband, yet highly efficient power combiner exploiting mix of open and short stub transmission line network. For single carrier CW operation, the proposed PA achieves 18.5-21.5 dBm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_{\text{sat}}$</tex>, 18-26% PAE across 106% bandwidth. We demonstrate one of the first concurrent multi-band mmWave modulation capability with three 32 QAM signals (total data rate up to 7.5 Gbps) across licensed/unlicensed spectrum of 36/39/66 GHz exhibiting 7.9/8.2/11.5 dBm linear average power and concurrent PAE of 11%. The PA exhibits one of the highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}_{\text{sat},3\text{dB}}$</tex> bandwidth with peak output power exceeding 20 dBm, peak PAE greater than 25%, and concurrent multi-band capability allowing new capabilities in spectrum sharing, frequency diversity and always connected capability in resource-constrained environment.

articleTitle: Characterization of GaN Recovery Effects under High-Power Pulsed RF Stress
abstract: This paper discusses the characterization of GaN transistors or MMICs under pulsed high-power stress and their recovery behaviour. A fully calibrated measurement setup is introduced where both forward and reflected waves are measured at input and output. In particular, also the effect of trapping due to the RF pulse on for example the insertion phase or input impedance can be measured. Measurement examples are shown on transistors from two different GaN technologies and compared to measurements on a GaAs transistor. Recovery measurements on GaN transistors in series and shunt configuration have been performed, showing in-depth the effects relevant for application of these devices in array environments.

articleTitle: Design of a 5G Application CML Frequency Divider for Improved Efficiency
abstract: An injection locked frequency divide-by-two current mode logic (CML) with injection directly through the bias tail current is implemented with reduced circuitry complexity and reduced power consumption. The proposed topology is capable of operating with a lower voltage supply compared to a conventional CML frequency divider topology with a maintained output voltage swing. A design guide for a given self-resonance frequency suitable for first cut design is proposed to estimate the optimal power consumption. A proof-of-concept of the proposed topology together with a conventional CML divider are implemented in an in-house BiCMOS process. The proposed topology occupies a silicon area of 0.0014 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and on-chip measurements show a locking range of 41.5 GHz, from 2 GHz to 43.5 GHz. The DC power consumption is 3.55 mW.

articleTitle: 20 GHz LNA and 29 GHz PA on SiGe BiCMOS technology for SatCom phased array systems
abstract: This paper presents a K-band single-ended Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) and a Ka-band single-ended Power Amplifier (PA) for a SatCom phased-array transceiver. The two circuits have been developed in 130-nm SiGe:C BiCMOS technology and fully characterized. In particular, the PA achieves 28.5 dB peak small-signal gain, 38.8 % peak power added efficiency (PAE), and an OIP3 better than 23.7 dBm within the entire operating frequency band. The maximum power consumption is 76 mW with a 2 V supply voltage, and it occupies an area of 1234 μm × 758 μm, pads included. The LNA achieves 33 dB peak power gain, 2.3 dB minimum noise figure, and -20 dBm IIP3 at 20 GHz. The NF, in the entire frequency band of interest, is less than 2.6 dB. It exhibits a power consumption of 20.7 mW with a supply voltage of 2.4 V and occupies an area of 1000 μm × 800 μm pads included.

articleTitle: Efficient EM-based variability analysis of passive microwave structures through parameterized reduced-order behavioral models
abstract: In this contribution we demonstrate how reduced-order behavioral models allow for extremely accurate and computationally efficient electromagnetic-based variability analysis of microwave passive structures. In particular, we report the MonteCarlo analysis of a wideband matching network at Ka-band, designed with a commercial foundry GaN-HEMT process PDK. As sources of variation we considered the thickness of the two dielectric layers available in the PDK to implement MIM capacitors of different order of magnitude, both exploited in the network. Based on a limited set of electromagnetic simulations, a parameterized behavioral model is extracted and then translated into a parameterized circuit equivalent (SPICE netlist) straightforward to be imported into RF CAD tools. The adopted model, implementing a rational approximation of the simulated S-parameters with rational dependence on the two parameters, provides excellent agreement with electromagnetic simulations, robustness against port impedance change and good extrapolation capabilities.

articleTitle: A Dual-Modulus Frequency Divider up to 128 GHz in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper describes a 2/3 dual-modulus frequency divider operating up to an input frequency of 128 GHz. It is built with emitter-coupled logic (ECL) based d-type flip-flops (DFFs) and AND gates, where the AND gates are merged with the input stages of the DFFs. Inductive shunt peaking is implemented to boost the speed performance. The dual-modulus divider consumes 28 mA from a 3.3 V supply. It is produced with the IHP's next generation SiGe:C BiCMOS technology SG13G3 with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\mathrm{t}}/f_{\max}$</tex> values of 470 GHz/610 GHz. The circuit constitutes a key component of a fully programmable frequency divider which is essential in phase-locked loops for mmWave communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: A 38-GHz Millimeter Wave Transmission System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle in 65 nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents the 38-GHz transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) chips applied in Unmaned Aerial Vehicle. Unlike the works in [1], [3]–[5] using Phased-Array approaches, the presented Tx and Rx uses single channel approaches to save the power. The Tx can provide 15 dBm saturated power with 16 dB gain under 0.425W and the Rx can provide 5 dB Noise Figure with 25 dB conversion gain under 0.53 W. Both Tx chip can achieve EVM of 2.6% rms under 4096-QAM using AI modeling.

articleTitle: A Broadband 110 – 170 GHz Frequency Quadrupler with 29 dBc Harmonic Rejection in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a differential frequency quadrupler (FQ) for future 6G wireless communications based on two cascaded bootstrapped Gilbert cells (GC) with a high broadband in-band harmonic rejection. This rejection is achieved through careful adjustment of the transmission line electrical length at the bootstrapped GC. The FQ is fabricated in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology with heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) with an f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> / f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 300 GHz and 450 GHz, respectively. The FQ covers the entire D-band from 110 to 170 GHz and delivers a maximum output power of +2.5 dBm with a peak gain of 11 dB and a high power-added efficiency (PAE) of up to 2.2%. Within the entire D-band, the FQ achieves a minimum harmonic rejection of 29 dBc, which - to the best of the author's knowledge - is the highest among any reported work at a comparable operational bandwidth without filters. The presented chip occupies an area of 0.7mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads and draws a DC current of 33 mA from a 3.3 V power supply.

articleTitle: TCAD-based Dynamic Thermal X-parameters for PA Self-Heating Analysis
abstract: TCAD simulations are used to extract an accurate temperature-dependent X-parameter active device model, which describes it as instantaneously dependent on the junction temperature, and hence represents the ideal framework to analyze device self-heating. Once exported from TCAD into EDA tools, X-parameters are coupled to a dynamic thermal impedance, leading to a compact and efficient device black-box model, allowing for circuit-level analysis of thermal memory effects in microwave circuits, like Power Amplifiers (PAs), even in presence of complex modulated-signal excitation. In particular, we focus on the thermal analysis of a class-A PA at E-band based on a 54 nm Si FinFET. The accuracy of the temperature-dependent X-parameter model is demonstrated first by comparing circuit simulations with TCAD results in continuous wave. Then we extend the analysis to pulsed modulated operation, highlighting thermal dynamic effects as a function of the pulse period.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Orthogonal Load-Modulated Balanced Amplifier in 22 nm CMOS FDSOI
abstract: An integrated orthogonal load-modulated balanced amplifier (OLMBA) is designed and fabricated using 22 nm CMOS FDSOI. The input control signal in OLMBA is reflected back to balanced power amplifier (PA) pair via reactively terminated quadrature hybrid at the output in order to achieve load modulation. The proposed PA operates at third generation partnership project/ne <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$w$</tex> radio (3GPP/NR) 26/28 GHz Frequency Range 2 (FR2), achieving 19.5 dBm output power, 16.6 dB gain, 15.7% power added efficiency (PAE) and 18.3 dBm output 1-dB compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{P}_{\text{1dB}})$</tex>, measured at 26 GHz. The PA shows excellent linearity performance with modulated signals. Using -28 dBc adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) and -21.9 dB (8%) error vector magnitude as threshold values, the proposed PA achieves 11.4 dBm and 4.9 dBm average output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{P}_{\text{avg}})$</tex> with 100 MHz and 400 MHz 64-QAM 3GPP/NR FR2 signal, and 14 dBm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{P}_{\text{avg}}$</tex> with 0.6 Gb/s (120 MHz) single carrier (SC) 64-QAM signal, measured at 26 GHz.

articleTitle: A 44 GHz-BW 18.5 GS/s Sampling Front-End Robust to Power Supply and Common-Mode Variations in 22 nm FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a pseudo-differential buffered front-end sampler (T&H) operating at 18.5 GS/s with 44 GHz measured signal bandwidth. The highly-linear sampler, intended for a 5-bit 4X time-interleaved (TI) 74 GS/s flash ADC, is realized in a 22 nm FD-SOI (FDX) CMOS process. It comprises an ultra-low jitter limiting clock path and a forward-body-biased source-follower based T&H architecture maximizing the overall linearity and effective sampling bandwidth, as well as achieving a differential input range of 600 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mV}_{\mathbf{ppd}}$</tex> by using a dual 1.2 V and 0.9 V supply voltage. The core T&H design has been presented in [1]. The ultra-wideband T&H design is highly insensitive to both power supplies (0.9V and 1.2V), as well as input common-mode variations. The obtained measurement results confirm robustness. The nominal SFDR and SNR remains well above 37.6 dBc and 39.3 dB (ENOB=5.49 bits), respectively, using a single-tone sine wave up to 39 GHz (5th Nyquist zone). Extended two-tone linearity characterizations reveal intermodulation products IM2 and IM3 of better than 44.5 and 40.5 dBc for a HF two-tone input at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{f}_{\text{in1}}=35.2$</tex> GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\text{in}2}=36.1$</tex> GHz. Across <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10{\%}$</tex> supply variations, the SNR and SFDR merely vary by 1 and 2 dB, respectively. The sensitivity to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10{\%}$</tex> input common-mode variations is even less than 1 dB for the same 39 GHz single-tone test. The compact differential design considering the input buffers, T&H core, clock buffer and low-jitter sample-phase occupies a core area as small as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.004\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex> in the utilized 22 nm FD-SOI process. The total power consumption is only 75mW of which 10mW is consumed by the entire clock path operating from the 0.9V supply.

articleTitle: A Mixer-Like Nonlinear Analysis for GaN HEMT Supply-Modulated Power Amplifier at 3.8 GHz
abstract: A nonlinear analysis of a GaN HEMT supply-modulated power amplifier (SMPA) based on the time-varying power series approach is presented. For this purpose, the SMPA operation is described as a drain mixer, in which the envelope signal plays the role of the local oscillator. The proposed analysis predicts the internal cancellation of intermodulation products, determined by nonlinear contributions occurring in the SMPA and identifies the responsible terms. The approach is based on the extraction of the requested parameters from dynamic I/V characteristics. This analysis is validated experimentally by a GaN HEMT SMPA operating at 3.8 GHz developed for this purpose, reporting a decrease of third-order intermodulation products in excess of 30 dB.

articleTitle: High Linearity 76-81 GHz LNA Using a 16 nm FinFET Technology for Phased Array Radar Applications
abstract: A highly linear 76–81 GHz Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) has been fabricated in a 16 nm FinFET CMOS process for phased array radar applications. The LNA includes two stages with a third order intermodulation distortion cancellation technique implemented on the second stage and ESD protection at the input of the first stage. The overall gain of the LNA is 17 dB with Input IP3 of 3dBm and Noise Figure (NF) of 4.5 dB. The total power consumption of the receiver is 31 mW and it has an exceptionally compact active area of 0.053 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,

articleTitle: On The Burn-in of GaN-on-Si MMIC High Power Amplifiers for SATCOM Applications
abstract: This paper deals with the burn-in and stability performance over time of some Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) High Power Amplifiers (HPAs) realized on a commercially available 100 nm gate length Gallium Nitride (GaN) on Silicon (Si) technology. In particular, the analysis involves two HPAs designed for the same application, i.e., satcom in the 17.3-20.2GHz Band, but based on different architectures, i.e. corporate and balance ones. Both designs are compliant with space reliability constraints and, despite the larger thermal resistance shown by the Si substrate with respect to the more common Silicon Carbide (SiC), they deliver up to 10 W of output power with about 30% of power added efficiency (PAE) and more than 23 dB of gain, from 17.3 GHz to 20.2 GHz. The MMICs have been subject of several tests carried out in continuous wave (CW) condition by monitoring endlessly (e.g., for 24 hours) their most relevant parameters i.e., output power, efficiency, gate and drain currents, in order to evaluate their stability over time. The registered results have shown almost negligible performance degradation, with the output power and PAE diminished of only 0.1 dB and 0.5%, respectively, thus revealing a significant maturity of the technology.

articleTitle: Wideband mmWave Transceiver IC for 5G Radios
abstract: A wideband <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.13\mu m$</tex> SiGe BiCMOS direct-conversion transceiver chip for 5G communications in the Ka-band is presented. The receiver (RX) includes low-noise amplifiers (LNA) with variable gain, a quadrature down-converter with gain control, an IQ local-oscillator (LO) generation network and an active IQ baseband (BB) filter with a 28-224MHz adjustable cut-off frequency. It achieves a 5.5dB noise figure (NF) and a maximum input-referred 3rd order intercept point (IIP3) of -1dBm while having a gain control range of 90dB. The transmitter (TX) is comprised of an active IQ baseband filter with programmable cut-off frequency between 90-720MHz, an IQ LO generation network, an IQ up-converter with gain control, LO leakage compensation and a variable gain amplifier (VGA). It attains 12.8dBm saturated output power (Psat) and 20dBm output-referred 3rd order intercept point (OIP3) for 14dB maximum voltage gain, while having a gain control range of 50dB. The transceiver has 8-11GHz LO input and consumes 540mW in receive mode and 500mW in transmit mode from 2.6V supply.

articleTitle: A 37-87 GHz Continuously Tunable Signal Source in a 130 nm SiGe:C BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a signal source with a continuous frequency tuning range of 50 GHz for high resolution FMCW radar systems in the lower millimeter wave region. The concept of the signal source is based on an ultra-wideband <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{K}_{\mathrm{u}}$</tex>-Band LC-VCO along with two cascaded bootstrapped Gilbert-Cell frequency doublers. The chip is fabricated in Infineon's BiCMOS production technology B11HFC which offers HBTs with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathbf{T}}$</tex> of 250 GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{f}_{\max}$</tex> of 370 GHz. The chip has a power consumption of only 241 mW and uses an area of 0.864 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The signal source reaches an absolute frequency tuning range (FTR) of 50 GHz (relative FTR=81%) at a center frequency of 62.2 GHz. The phase noise at 1 MHz offset is as low as -95 dBc/Hz. The output level is around 3 dBm.

articleTitle: GaAs MMIC Interferometer for Broadband Interference Suppression
abstract: This paper presents a GaAs interference suppression MMIC for integration in broadband receiver front ends. The circuit is an interferrometer, with a gain stage in one path, and a gain stage followed by a variable delay line in the other path. The voltage-tunable delay is implemented with discrete inductors and diode-connected transistors. The total time delay of the second path is adjusted by varying the voltage on the varactors to place a spectral notch at different frequencies across the band. The demonstrated prototype circuit is well matched across X-band and the notch can be tuned from 8.2 to 10.8 GHz. For a CW signal in this band, the circuit shows a 10 dB suppression of interference signals 2 GHz away, and over 11 dB suppression for 3 GHz separation. Broadband suppression at the front end can improve the useful dynamic range of digital cancellation.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band GaN 2x4 MMIC Switch for compact and scalable Switch Matrices
abstract: This paper describes the design and experimental results of a DP4<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> MMIC switch to be used as a building block for high-order compact and scalable Ka-band Switch Matrices. Two variants of the MMIC have been designed and optimized to be used in bare-die form, within hermetic complex modules, and in QFN plastic package solution, to be assembled in PCB based architectures. Both chips are manufactured on a European 0.15 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> GaN/SiC HEMT technology for a total die area of 4x4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Good equalized insertion losses of about 2.5 and 3.5 dB, for bare-die and packaged variants respectively, were measured along all possible active paths. A minimum isolation level of 30 dB and a return loss better than 15 dB at all the RF ports were achieved for both circuits. The MMICs are fully compliant with the space deratings.

articleTitle: A Q/V Band Low Noise Amplifier using Space de-rated Bias Conditions
abstract: In this paper we present a low noise amplifier (LNA) designed under space de-rating conditions reaching an average noise figure of 1.45 dB within a frequency range of 44 to 50 GHz and 1.55 dB from 40 to 50 GHz. Inside the targeted bandwidth of 47 to 54 GHz the gain is 26 dB with a gain variation less than 1.2 dB over the entire frequency band. Additionally to the low noise figure the LNA is featuring a 1-dB compression point above 10 dBm over the entire bandwidth by using a large gate-width output transistor.

articleTitle: 108 and 124 GHz Fundamental VCOs with 21% and 7% DC-to-RF Efficiency in 22nm CMOS FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents the design of two high efficiency fundamental voltage controlled oscillators (VCO) for sub-THz applications. The design optimizes the transistor for voltage gain, swing and PAE at the operating frequency to achieve 21% and 7% DC-to-RF efficiencies. The varactor and back-gate voltages are utilized for tuning control. The back-gate controls improves the relative tuning range of the VCOs by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 50%. Layout techniques are employed in the transistor and inductor to improve the VCO frequency. The two VCOs are implemented in 22nm CMOS FDSOI, oscillate at 108.7 GHz and 124 GHz having an output power of 3.41 and -1.45 dBm with a tuning range of 3.4% and 3.7%, respectively. The chip operates at a supply voltage of 0.7V and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{BIAS}$</tex> of 1.4mA with a core power consumption of 10.2mW and 9.9mW, respectively. The active area is 0.095x0.087 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mm^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A New Architecture of Broadband GaAs MMIC Balanced Mixer for Very High RF/IF Isolation for 0.5-18.5 GHz Signal Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a new architecture of balanced passive mixer aimed at providing very high bandwidth and very high isolation between RF and IF ports. The architecture is based on a double Marchand balun that allows routing the interconnection between the quad-transistors terminals such that the overlaps and misalignment between interconnections are avoided. The paper presents a mixer prototype fully integrated in 0.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> GaAs p-HEMT process and is capable to convert signal in the the 0.5-18.5 GHz bandwidth into the 6–12 GHz bandwidth. Measurement reports a conversion gain between -3.5 dB and -6.5 dB and an isolation between RF (input) and IF (output) between 36 dB and 42 dB, while an LO isolation to output port in excess of 40 dB.

articleTitle: A 55-GHz Highly Linear Direct-Conversion RF Transmitter in 40 nm CMOS
abstract: A 55-GHz direct-conversion RF transmitter with high linearity and quadrature mismatch calibration is presented. The RF transmitter comprises a power amplifier, image-rejection quadrature mixer, baseband amplifier, and quadrature VCO. To achieve a highly linear output power per die area, we employ a distributed active transformer-based two-way power-combining power amplifier, and a pFET-based passive mixer. The I/Q mismatch calibration is implemented for a high image-rejection ratio. The amplitude mismatch is calibrated by tuning the gate biases of the mixer switching FETs, and the phase mismatch is calibrated by 3-bit switched capacitor tuning at the LO buffer LC load. Realized in 40 nm CMOS with a die area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1.6}\times \boldsymbol{0.7}\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>, the RF transmitter exhibits <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{OP}_{\mathbf{1dB}}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+\boldsymbol{12.8}\mathbf{dBm}, \mathbf{P}_{\mathbf{sat}}$</tex> of +13.9 dBm, IRR of -45.2 dBc, LOFT of -36.3 dBc. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{OP}_{1\mathbf{dB}}$</tex> per die area is 17 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: 46% Peak PAE 28 GHz High Linearity Stacked-FET Power Amplifier IC with a Novel Two-Step Adaptive Bias Circuit in 45-nm SOI CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a 28 GHz high linearity power amplifier (PA) IC with a novel two-step adaptively controlled bias circuit for 5th generation (5G) mobile terminal applications in a 45-nm silicon on insulator (SOI) CMOS process. The novel bias circuit adaptively controls the gate voltage of a stacked-FET by a step procedure to improve the 1dB compression point (P1dB) and efficiency in the several-dB back-off region. The PA employs a 3-stacked-FET structure to overcome the low breakdown voltage issue in scaled MOSFETs. At a supply voltage of 3.5 V, the fabricated PA exhibits a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 46.0%, a saturated output power of 20.5 dBm, a 3 dB output power back-off efficiency of 35.2%, a 6 dB output power back-off efficiency of 26.0% and a small signal gain of 15.0 dB. The PA IC occupies only 0.23 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Counter-Intermodulation in the Context of CMOS Outphasing Transmitters
abstract: This work presents the design of a CMOS outphasing modulator based on an IQ-modulator topology with passive mixers. The implications from such an architecture on the phase-modulator performance are analysed. Particularly, the problem of counter-intermodulation in the context of outphasing modulation is studied. It is found that the generated distortion is a function of the outphasing angle. Based on the analysis, a 65-nm CMOS prototype is designed and fabricated. Measurements show an ACLR performance of -46.7 dB and -42.5 dB for a 64-QAM modulated signal with a 5MHz and 40MHz bandwidth, respectively.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Down-Conversion Mixer with RF Back-Gate Excitation Topology in 22-nm FD-SOI
abstract: This paper presents a novel 28 GHz down-conversion mixer topology using the back-gate terminal in 22 nm FD-SOI as an RF excitation port for the 21 GHz local oscillator (LO) signal. A double balanced architecture with an active load and transimpedance amplifier were implemented in the 22FDX® technology from GlobalFoundries. The mixing functionality is provided at the level of a single FET, that is simultaneously excited at the front- and back-gates by the RF and LO signals, respectively. Under 0.9 V power supply (26 mW DC consumption) the proposed down-conversion mixer exhibits a maximum conversion gain of 3.5 dB by applying 10 dBm of LO power. The 1 dB compression point occurs at -6 dBm of RF input power and the third order intercept (IIP3) point is 15 dBm at nominal LO power. Benchmarking these values against mixer performances from the literature reveals this design to be close to the current state-of-the-art in CMOS and SOI technology, demonstrating the viability of this novel topology employing back-gate excitation at mm-wave frequencies

articleTitle: Demonstration of 300-nm InP/GaInAsSb DHBT MMIC Technology in a 60-160GHz Ultra-Broadband Amplifier Test Vehicle
abstract: We demonstrate an InP/GaInAsSb DHBT MMIC technology with a 300-nm emitter size. As a test vehicle, ultra-broadband 60–160 GHz amplifiers were fabricated and characterized. The transistors rely on a 20-nm-thick compositionally- and dopant-graded quaternary GaInAsSb base layer which leads to high breakdown-voltage BV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CEO</inf> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(> 5.3\ \mathrm{V})$</tex> and high cut-off frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{\mathrm{T}} > 520 \ \text{and}f_{\text{MAX}} > 700\ \text{GHz})$</tex>. This base design enables higher DC-biasing points as well as higher RF output power levels, making quaternary-based DHBTs well-suited for mm- and sub-mm-wave amplification. One-stage and two-stage amplifiers were designed and fabricated. The small-signal RF gain of the one- and two-stage amplifiers are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 7$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 13$</tex> dB up to 110 GHz, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 7$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 9$</tex> dB up to 160 GHz. The one- and two-stage amplifiers deliver 8 and 10 dBm POUT at 94 GHz with a DC power consumption of only 34 and 90 m<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: A 8–18 GHz Low Noise Variable Gain Amplifier with 30 dB Gain Control Range
abstract: This brief presents a single-stage current steering, low noise variable gain amplifier with a novel amplitude and phase error reduction method. The design is implemented in IHP's 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS technology for 8–18 GHz. At the highest gain setting, S21 is 12.4 dB, the minimum noise figure is 1.93 dB, and the maximum input 1-dB compression point is 3.9 dBm. Fine gain control steps are achieved up to 30 dB with 0.5 dB increments. The maximum measured rms phase and amplitude errors are 12.3° and 0.49 dB, respectively. The proposed design consumes 24 mW DC power and occupies 0.58 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads. To the best of the authors' knowledge, our work achieves the lowest noise figure and highest IP <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dB</inf> are achieved among the published variable gain amplifiers.

articleTitle: 150-nm GaN HEMT Degradation under Realistic Load-Line Operation
abstract: In this paper, reliability issues in Gallium Nitride (GaN) HEMTs are empirically investigated. To this purpose, stress measurements were carried out on a microwave transistor under realistic load-line conditions exploiting a nonlinear load-pull setup operating at few megahertz. Although the characterization strategy was applied on a 150-nm GaN technology, it has general validity and, as will be demonstrated by the reported experimental results, can be successfully applied to evaluate the maturity of the investigated technology processes.

articleTitle: An assembly process oriented thermal-mechanical characterization of a fan-out wafer-level package
abstract: This study focuses on the stress analysis using finite element methods regarding a wafer-level Cu pillar package assembly process. The detailed assembly process is described, and a process-oriented thermal-mechanical coupled model is developed as the stress analysis tool. The finite element analysis is divided into two sections, namely the identification of the critical assembly step, and the analysis of the critical stress development. The package dimension and material property variables are parametrized by taking all the possibilities that could happen in the assembly process into consideration. The influence of each parameter is characterized and critical parameters are addressed, together with some initial assembly test results taken as validations. It is found that the most critical step for the solder is the reflow process, and the most critical stresses are the Cu pillar solder shear stress as well as the solder ball tensile stress.

articleTitle: Differential Coupler Topologies for Built-In Self-Test of SiGe Automotive Radar Transceivers
abstract: This paper presents two differential directional coupler topologies for millimeter-wave built-in self-test (BIST) in the 76 GHz to 81 GHz automotive radar band. One structure is weakly-coupled with a coupling factor (CF) of 21.5 dB, which corresponds to a minimal insertion loss of only 0.3 dB in the signal path under test. The second structure features a tighter coupling of 9.6 dB with an insertion loss around 2 dB. Measured sample-to-sample and frequency variation of the coupling factor are below 0.8 dB for the weakly-coupled and 0.2 dB for the tightly-coupled topology, facilitating accurate power measurement in the BIST. To minimize BIST overhead, the area footprint is kept compact. A generic approach to layout ensures that the couplers can be re-used in various parts of the circuit under test to minimize design time.

articleTitle: 5 Watts, MMIC, K-Band Doherty PA for Satellite Communications
abstract: This work presents the first MMIC voltage-mode Doherty PA. The presented PA exploits a symmetric Doherty PA topology with a distinct compact power combiner. The proposed concept is validated by designing and measuring a prototype for the frequency range 17.3 GHz to 19.3 GHz. The fabricated prototype demonstrates a peak output power of 37.2 dBm with 5 dB to 6 dB efficiency backoff with at least 24% power-added efficiency (PAE) at 32 dBm backoff output power.

articleTitle: Inductorless 96 Gb/s PAM-4 Optical Modulators Driver in SiGe:C BiCMOS
abstract: In this paper, an inductorless PAM-4 driver for optical modulators fabricated in IHP's 130nm SG13G2 SiGe:C BiCMOS technology is presented. The driver, based on a 2-bit current-mode DAC topology, delivers 2.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\text{pp}}$</tex> voltage swing over a differential 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> while consuming 197mW power, for a power efficiency of 2.87 %. Bandwidth enhancement through capacitive peaking ensures a broad 50 GHz 3 dB bandwidth keeping at the same time a small footprint. Time domain measurements demonstrate how the driver is able to deliver a 48GBd PAM-4 signal, corresponding to a bit rate of 96 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Microstrip GaAs Power Amplifiers for High Capacity 92–114 GHz 5G and 6G Backhaul
abstract: Single-ended and balanced 90–115 GHz microstrip amplifiers have been designed for cost-sensitive 5G and 6G backhaul in a new, commercial 6-inch, 0.1-μm GaAs process. At 108 GHz, measured output power is 20.4 and 22.5 dBm, respectively, which is among the highest reported for microstrip amplifiers at this frequency and competitive with expensive GaN processes. Good agreement is shown with simulation.

articleTitle: A 30-GHz CMOS LC VCO with Optimal Tail Filter Considering Tail FET's Output Resistance
abstract: A low phase-noise and wide tuning-range 30-GHz CMOS LC VCO based on the tail-current-biased cross-coupled nFET structure is designed for Ka-band applications. An RC low-pass filter at the tail FET's gate node boosts the output resistance over a wide range of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS,</inf> as well as suppresses the output noise of the tail FET. It consequently improves the phase noise when combined with an LC tail filter. An inter-stage LC filter at VCO-buffer interface boosts the swing at the buffer input to avoid unwanted phase noise degradation. An optimal placement and routing are designed to compactly embed the proposed LC and RC filters into the entire layout. Realized in 65 nm CMOS, the VCO covers 29.9-34.5 GHz with four sub-bands, while consuming 14.1 mA from 1.2 V. It exhibits the phase noise of -108.7 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset with 31.3 GHz output frequency, resulting in FoM of -187.5 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz Doherty PA with 22.9% PAEmax and 17.4% PAE at 6-dB PBO in 0.13μm SiGe Technology for 5G Application
abstract: This paper presents an mm-wave Doherty PA in a Infineon 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS for output power and back-off efficiency optimization for 5G communications. The output stage of the main PA and the auxiliary PA use a stacked topology for high output power without trading the power gain. A voltage-combiner with a transformer-based output matching network is proposed to achieve a true Doherty load modulation in a wide signal bandwidth while maintaining a compact layout. The PA is fabricated with Infineon 0.13 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> SiGe BiCMOS technology with a core area of 0.36 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. At 5G 28 GHz, the measured OP1db is 22.9 dBm, and PAE at 6-dB PBO is 17.4%. At 28 GHz with 400 MHz bandwidth, it shows an EVM of 5% with average output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{P}_{\text{avg}})$</tex> of 15.32 dBm with 14.6% PAE.

articleTitle: Scalable, Modular Feed-Forward Equalizer for Baseband Applications
abstract: This paper presents a modular and scalable fully differential Feed-Forward Equalizer topology suitable for baseband applications. The proposed equalizer topology utilizes Gilbert cell amplifiers as variable gain elements and follows a modular implementation with reuse of identical gain cells. A proof of concept one-tap Feed-Forward Equalizer is designed, characterized in frequency and time domain measurements. The equalizer exhibits a measured single-ended peaking gain control of up to 27 dB at 50 GHz. The equalizer MMIC consumes 370 mW from a -3.3 V supply, measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.94\ \mathrm{x}\ 0.76\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, and it was designed in Infineon's 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{t}$</tex> of 250 GHz and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{max}$</tex> of 370 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Power InP Resonant Tunnelling Diode Heterostructure for 300-GHz Oscillator Sources
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> high-power double-barrier resonant tunnelling diode (RTD) epitaxial structure in InP technology is reported. The heterostructure exhibits moderate available current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta J\simeq 1.4\ \text{mA}/\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> and large voltage swing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta V\simeq 1.2$</tex> V, resulting in a maximum RF power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{RF,\max}\simeq 0.31\ \text{mW}/u\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, and over 530 GHz bandwidth, being 25 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, 36 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex>, and 49 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex> large RTD devices expected to deliver up to 5 mW, 7 mW, and 10 mW at 300 GHz, respectively. Distributed inductors in both coplanar and microstrip geometry are designed through full 3D electromagnetic simulations, proving the feasibility of the proposed approach for the practical realisation of high-power 300-GHz oscillator sources employing low-cost optical lithography.

articleTitle: A 79 GHz reconfigurable highly linear Low-Noise Amplifier for Civil-Automotive Short-Range-Radars in 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable highly linear low-noise amplifier (LNA) for civil-automotive radars in the predefined automotive short-range-radar (SRR) band from 77 GHz to 81 GHz. A simple two-bit control for gain and linearity is implemented, making this circuit very adaptive to different applications scenarios. A reconfigurable cascode stage with capacitive neutralization in its common-source (CS) is employed as amplifier core. By tuning the voltage at the back-gate (BG) terminal of the CS transistors, the gain and input-referred 1 dB-compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{iP}_{\mathbf{1dB}})$</tex> can be easily adjusted. Two of these tunable cores are cascaded providing a two-bit resolution over a wide tuning range. A transformer-based Marchand balun is designed and placed at the input and output to enable the circuit characterization in the target frequency range with the available single-ended laboratory instrumentation. The measurements of the fabricated chips show a tunable gain with BG voltage from 14 dB to 20.4 dB, while the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{iP}_{\mathbf{1dB}}$</tex> ranges from -4.5 dBm to -11 dBm, and the minimum noise figure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{NF}_{\min})$</tex> varies from 6.6 dB to 5.9 dB, respectively. Compared to the state of the art for LNAs operating at about 80 GHz, the presented circuit shows a very good performance with the highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{iP}_{\mathbf{1dB}}$</tex> and gain at the corresponding tuning boundaries, resulting in the best figure-of-merit.

articleTitle: A 10-GHz Single-Supply GaAs MMIC Self-Synchronous Rectifier
abstract: This paper presents an E-mode HEMT MMIC rectifier based on the design of a class-B power amplifier (PA) using the WIN 150nm PIH1 GaAs process. The PA simulations show over 40% PAE from approximately 9 to 11GHz with an input power of 12 dBm. Using time-reversal duality, a self-synchronous power rectifier (PR) is designed by modifying the PA so that the drain RF output becomes the input, while the RF input at the gate is terminated in a tunable high-reflection coefficient load. The drain bias line is terminated in an optimal DC load. The MMIC is measured with CW and several types of modulated signals. Peak rectifier conversion efficiency in CW operation is measured to be 60% at 10 GHz at 17 dBm input RF power. Peak rectifier efficiency at 10GHz with the same total input power is found to be 62% using a uniformly-distributed AM noise signal with a 50% modulation depth.

articleTitle: Checking Rollett's Proviso for Degenerated Devices through S-Parameter Analysis
abstract: An analysis is presented of the small-signal stability of the class of three-port networks derived by making the reference node of a two-port accessible. That class of networks is of particular interest since it includes, under rather mild conditions, any high-frequency active device when viewed as a three-port, i.e., when accessed also from the source (or emitter) terminal. The discussion here presented is completely based on a black-box (S-parameter) representation of the original two-port network, rather than on its small-signal equivalent circuit (SSEC). In a sense, this study complements a previous paper addressing small-signal active device stability from a SSEC standpoint. On the other hand, it is more general (not being based on a specific circuit topology) and more easy-to-use (not requiring the knowledge of the SSEC).

articleTitle: A 33-37GHz Phase-Aligning Frequency Generator with $3.5^{\circ}$ Accuracy and 20ns Switching Time
abstract: This work presents a mm-wave signal generation method that provides background phase tuning and self-alignment between adjacent sources. We validate the proposed method with a 2-element prototype in a 65nm CMOS process. The prototype has a chip area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3\text{mm}\times 2\text{mn}$</tex> and consumes a total DC power of 258mW. Chip measurements demonstrate a phase tuning range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$140^{\circ}$</tex> at 35GHz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20^{\circ}$</tex> /step and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 4^{\circ}$</tex> of RMS phase error. The measured phase switching time is 20ns. The measured phase noise at 1MHz offset is below -117dBc/Hz across the 33.5-37GHz bandwidth and the accumulated jitter is 85fs. This work provides a phase alignment technique for large-scale mm-wave phased arrays.

articleTitle: A W-Band Transmitter in 0.13um SiGe Technology
abstract: This paper presents a W-band transmitter front-end implemented in 0.13um SiGe BiCMOS technology. The transmitter consists of a driver amplifier, a phase shifter, a power amplifier, and input and output balun. A differential cascode structure is used in the driver amplifier and power amplifier design for improved gain and reverse isolation. W-band on-chip transformers are discussed in detail, which are widely used to realize low-loss and ultra-compact passive matching networks. This design strategy enables the entire transmitter core to fit within a 665 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}\times 266\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> die area. The transmitter is well matched within the design frequency band, achieving 12 dB of gain at 94 GHz and a total power consumption of 138 mW.

articleTitle: High frequency GaN HEMT Modeling with ASM-HEMT
abstract: Numerous CAD models are proposed today in the literature for GaN HEMT devices. They all have their place in circuit design. It just depends on which type of criteria and properties that the models should be able to simulate. Indeed, a physic-based model is very useful in the design phase of the device design, but unfortunately you will not have access to the structure of the transistor. Moreover, the use of this model in harmonic balance simulation will be limited due to the time consuming and non-convergence. Other models are mainly based on empirical or equivalent circuit approach. In the last ten years, a new type of models has appeared. Based on the definition of the surface potential [1] [2], they represent a good alternative to other modelling approach especially in terms of scalability and model performance [3] for applications where accurate distortion modeling is of paramount importance.

articleTitle: MMIC Up-Down-Converter with Integrated Band-Pass Filter for 5G mm-Wave Measurement Applications
abstract: 5G mm-wave applications are becoming more dominant in consumer and industry applications. The development of these applications requires advanced mm-wave measurement components, which allow a precise and fast characterization of devices under tests (DUTs). In this work we present a passive MMIC up-down-converter for the Ka-band, which implements an on-chip band-pass and low-pass filter. This design shows a very high LO to RF port isolation, while maintaining a low conversion loss and good conversion reciprocity.

articleTitle: Stabilisation and burn-in of X-band GaN HPA MMICs for space applications
abstract: This paper reports on the stabilisation and burn-in of X-band GaN HPA MMICs that are used in the Solid State Power Amplifier modules of an X-band multi-beam active antenna developed in the frame of ESA's PACIS3 Partnership Project between the satellite operator, HISDESAT and the European Space Agency (ESA). Test results that were extended to 2000 hours confirm excellent stability of the selected space evaluated GaN GH25-10 process as well as suitability of the stabilisation and burn-in strategy adopted for the manufacturing of the flight units.

articleTitle: A V-band Double-Transformer-Coupling and Current Steering VGLNA in 90-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a broadband (50-67GHz) variable gain low noise amplifier (VGLNA) with low dc power in 90-nm CMOS technology. A double-transformer-coupling (DTC) technique is used to improve gain and noise performance of the LNA. The variable gain function is implemented using a combination of DTC and current steering (DTCCS) techniques. With DTCCS technique, not only the power consumption can be reduced, but also the variable gain function can be implemented. The measured peak gain is 17.1 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth that covers from 50 to 67 GHz, and an 8-dB gain control range. The measured minimum noise figure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(NF)}$</tex> is 5.8 dB. The measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{IP}_{\mathbf{1dB}}$</tex> at the high gain state is -25 dBm. The VGLNA consumes only 5.7-mW dc power with a compact chip area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.6\times 1}\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Non-Uniform Distributed GaN LO Amplifier for Wideband 5–38 GHz Applications
abstract: A wideband LO amplifier is designed using a single-stage non-uniform distributed topology that contains 10 cells with varied 0.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> GaN HEMT peripheries interconnected by tapered gate and drain lines to provide improved large signal terminations to the transistors. Non-uniform capacitive division is incorporated at all cell gates for increased bandwidth, while gate resistors are tailored to ensure stability and produce a bias path. Simulated performance and probed measurements show that for the first time a GaN MMIC PA with more than 35 dBm maximum output power, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< \boldsymbol{2}$</tex> dB of gain ripple, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> \boldsymbol{15\%}$</tex> PAE has been demonstrated for a 5–38 GHz bandwidth at the die level. For packaged measurements at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{P}_{in}=\boldsymbol{28}$</tex> dBm, the 2.3 mm x 3.0 mm amplifier measured (including package losses) an average of 32.5 dBm output power and 5 dB gain with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> \boldsymbol{10\%}$</tex> PAE from 5–35 GHz, where the upper end of the band was limited by the external fixture.

articleTitle: A 2.5-2.6 dB Noise Figure LNA for 39 GHz band in 22 nm FD-SOI with Back-Gate Bias Tunability
abstract: This paper presents a 2-stage low-noise amplifier (LNA) designed in 22 nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) technology, covering the N259 and N260 millimeter-wave 5G bands. The prototype features 19.9 dB peak gain, 2.5-2.6 dB noise figure (NF) and 6.6 GHz bandwidth (intersection of 3 dB gain flatness and -10 dB input/output matching), -5.4 dBm third-order input intercept point (IIP3) for a 20.8 mW power dissipation. Modulating the back-gate bias of each stage independently switches the LNA operation mode from a combination of low-noise (0.8 dB variation in NF), high-linearity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 3$</tex> dB variation in IIP3) and/or low-power (down to 7.4 mW). Finally, a careful noise contribution analysis of the input matching identifies a 0.58 dB main contribution from the input spiral inductor. EM simulations show that a 0.06 dB improvement in NF can be achieved by using a high-resistivity substrate, if the input inductor design is optimized by stacking several metal layers.

articleTitle: Surface and Buffer Trap Signatures in Fe-doped AlGaN/GaN HEMT Identified by LF S-parameter TCAD Simulations
abstract: In this paper, the trap signatures located at the GaN cap/SiN interface and in the GaN buffer are clearly identified in the Fe-doped AlGaN/GaN HEMT device by means of low frequency (LF) S-parameter characteristics. For that, LF S-parameter TCAD Sentaurus physics-based 2D simulations are performed for different temperatures ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. In fact, the imaginary part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y_{22}$</tex> allows to extract the buffer trap parameters, while the imaginary part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Y}_{21}$</tex> provides a quantitative information of the traps located at both surface and buffer regions. An excellent agreement between measurement and simulation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Y}_{21}$</tex> parameter is obtained in this work. An activation energy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}=0.45$</tex> eV and a cross section around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{\mathrm{n}}=3\times 10^{\text{-}16}\ \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> are identified for buffer traps. The computed parameters for the surface traps are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ED} =\sim 0.3$</tex> eV and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma 0=\sim 5\times 10^{\text{-}18}\ \text{cm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Compact Patch-like Bandpass Filter using grounded CSRR on BiCMOS 55nm technology
abstract: This paper presents a design perspective of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order patch-like grounded Complementary-Split-Ring-Resonator (CSRR) filter on BiCMOS 55-nm technology at 50 GHz. The advantage of using CSRR topology combined with grounded via allows a great reduction of the overall size to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda/7\times\lambda/13}\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>. General coupling matrix representation along with extracted external quality factor and resonators' pair coupling is conducted. The measured results show an insertion loss of 5 dB with a return loss better than 11 dB in the passband. The achieved fractional bandwidth is 23%.

articleTitle: Compact High-Gain Driver Amplifier MMICs for 60 nm GaN-on-Si W-Band Single-Chip Transceivers
abstract: This paper presents compact W-band driver amplifier (DA) MMICs fabricated in a 60 nm GaN-on-Si process. The measured small-signal gain of single-stage, 4-stage and 6-stage DA circuits is equal to 1.9-4.3 dB, 10.7-17.5 dB and 14.0-25.1 dB at 77.5-100 GHz when the drain voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{d}})$</tex> is 7.5 V and the drain current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{d}})$</tex> is equal to 40/140/230 mA. The 6-stage DA circuit has a measured output power of 10.9-17.2 dBm with 8.5-16.0 dB of power gain at 77.5-100 GHz when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{d}}=10$</tex> V and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{d}}=230$</tex> mA. The multi-stage DAs have attractive features such as small circuit sizes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1.6-2.2\ \text{mm}^{2})$</tex> and high gain in a wide frequency range at W-band. The 6-stage driver amplifier can be a more area-efficient option in 60 nm GaN-on-Si W-band single-chip transceivers or transmitters due to its compact size, comparably high gain and output power in a relatively wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: GaN SPA-D with 8-dB Back-Off for Wideband mm-Wave Applications
abstract: We present the first fully integrated sequential power amplifier with Doherty-type active load modulation (SPA-D). The design methodology unveils that wideband implementations with constantly high power added efficiency (PAE) for large back-offs (BO) are realisable with mm-wave power amplifiers. An asymmetric 2-stage 2-way SPA-D from 17.3 GHz to 20.3 GHz is fabricated in a 0.15 μm GaN process. Experimental results demonstrate peak envelope powers (PEP) > 36 dBm with 36 % PAE. At 8-dB BO 33 % PAE is achieved.

articleTitle: Development and RF-Performance of AlGaN/GaN and InAlN/GaN HEMTs on Large-Diameter High-Resistivity Silicon Substrates
abstract: A CMOS-compatible industrial processing and RF analysis of 150 mm GaN-on-HR-Si substrates with AlGaN and InAlN barrier is presented. Process development along with transfer to large-wafer scale is shown and some HEMT calibration devices produced on AlGaN/GaN following the aforementioned procedure are characterized in terms of RF-performance by using a set of measured multi-bias <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>-parameters. An automatic small-signal equivalent circuit extraction strategy for these AlGaN/GaN DUTs is validated and some de-embedded figures of merit, namely <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\mathbf{T}}\approx$</tex> 20 GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\boldsymbol{\max}}\approx$</tex> 41 GHz are drawn out for initial evaluation of the technology.

articleTitle: A Miniature 100V, 130W Multi-Octave UHF GaN on SiC Transistor with Internal Feedback
abstract: A 100V GaN on SiC transistor measuring just 0.39 x 0.23” is reported that operates over the full 100–500 MHz frequency range with a minimum of 130W output power and 52% efficiency. This is believed to be the first report of the use of 100V GaN HEMT technology for multi-octave applications. A unique feature of the design is the incorporation of feedback within the transistor package for>100W operation.

articleTitle: A 315 GHz Source with Integrated Antenna in InP-DHBT Technology
abstract: A 315-GHz source with integrated antenna is presented. It consists of a harmonic oscillator and a patch antenna. The harmonic oscillator is realized based on the push-push topology using a 0.8 μm-emitter transferred-substrate (TS) InP-DHBT technology with an fmax of 320 GHz. The harmonic oscillator together with antenna delivers -10 dBm of output power. DC power consumption is only 21 mW from a 1.6-volt power supply, which corresponds to 0.5% overall DC-to-RF efficiency. The chip area of the source with integrated antenna circuit is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.9\times 0.65$</tex> mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz Four-Element Beam-Tapering Receive Phased Array
abstract: A 60-GHz four-element beam-tapering receive phased array is proposed in this study. The proposed receive phased array channel cover a phase control range of 360° using a 3-bit 180° phase shifter and a phase invertible low noise amplifier (PILNA) to achieve low power consumption and high gain. Moreover, by applying the beam-tapering technique without additional DC power consumption through a passive attenuator, interference from unwanted direction can be suppressed. The receive phased array fabricated in 65-nm CMOS process occupies a size of 2.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. From the measurement results, the proposed circuit shows an average peak gain of 26.1 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth of 15 GHz from 52 to 67 GHz, covering 360° phase control range with a 22.5° phase resolution. Between 57 to 67 GHz, the RMS phase and gain errors during gain control are less than 7° and 1.25 dB, respectively. Furthermore, by providing 5-dB of gain control through the attenuator with less than 4° phase error, the beam-tapering function can be supported.

articleTitle: Switched shield mm-wave tunable slow wave CPW in FinFET CMOS technology
abstract: This paper presents slow wave transmission lines in a 16 nm CMOS technology, including a tunable slow wave CPW. They are measured up to 67 GHz. Electromagnetic simulation combined with parasitic extraction and characterization-based transistor models predict accurately phase constant. Attenuation is harder to simulate and requires silicon verification. The tunability is achieved by modifying the connection to the shield of the line using highly scaled FinFET MOS transistors as switching elements, leaving 65% of the area under the top metals free. Phase constant difference is 20.5 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>/mm at 50 GHz, with a maximum attenuation constant of 2.3 dB/mm for a line width of 48 μm.

articleTitle: 3D EM Multi-technology simulation flow for GaN and RF-SOI heterogeneous integration technique
abstract: This paper presents a novel 3D EM multi-technology simulation flow applied to the Micro-Transfer Printing (MTP) heterogeneous integration technique between GaN and RF-SOI. A modular approach is proposed which relies on the two technology PDKs, the definition of a Cu-RDL technology and an assembly library. This flow addresses the intricate nature of the conformal RDL between the two technologies. Additionally, it offers a complete traceability, physical verification as well as EM simulation environment. The flow is verified with two MTP demonstrators, a CPW transmission line and a DC-6GHz SPDT switch. A good hardware/model correlation is observed which validate the proposed flow.

articleTitle: A D-band, High Switching Speed, Differential Reflection-Type Phase Shifter in 250-nm InP HBT
abstract: A high switching speed differential reflection-type phase shifter (RTPS) is presented for operation in D-band. A differential topology is adopted to isolate the RF signal leaking through the control path as well as employing a virtual ground for wider control bandwidth. Fabricated in a 250-nm InP HBT process, the 360° phase shift range is achieved across 110 GHz - 163 GHz with two cascaded RTPS stages. The measured insertion loss at 110 GHz is -13.4±5dB with modulation bandwidth of 5 GHz.

articleTitle: A third order analogue pre-distorter MMIC for E-band PA linearisation
abstract: In this paper we present the design, characterisation and non-linear control of an analogue pre-distortion (APD) MMIC at E-band. With non-linear behaviour models of the APD MMIC, we demonstrate the capability of controlling the quadrature gain and quadrature third order term. Finally, the APD is combined with a 1 W E-band PA, where we by cascading their measured responses show overall more linear behaviour towards saturated output power compared with the non-linearised 1 W PA. Simulated with 256 QAM modulated signals, the average output power of the linearised PA was 22.2 dBm in comparison to 18.7 dBm.

articleTitle: A High Linearity 6 GHz LNA in 130 nm SiGe Technology
abstract: In this work, a high linearity LNA at 6 GHz with 1.15 dB NF, 27.7 dB gain is reported with IHP 130nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The reported LNA achieves a highly linear performance and has -12.2 dBm IP1dB and 4.2 dBm IIP3. A two-stage cascode amplifier with inductive degeneration topology is used to obtain high gain. Optimum transistor biasing and sizing achieves an input matching without using any inductor which allowed low NF and high linearity. Additionally, custom, not PDK defined, transistor layouts have been created to decrease the core's parasitics to enhance the LNA's performance. LNA uses 3.3V as supply and consumes 98 mW DC power while occupying a 0.75 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> die area without pads. The reported LNA achieved one of the highest figures-of-merit among silicon-based LNAs and has comparable performance to SOI CMOS LNAs.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Wide Gain Control Range CMOS Variable Gain Amplifier Using PMOS for 5G Communications
abstract: This paper presents the variable gain amplifier (VGA) implemented in a 65 nm RF CMOS process. It works in Ka-band for 5G Communication, with wide bandwidth, low RMS phase error, and wide gain control range performance. A shunt resistor was used to create a low Q inductor for wide bandwidth. In addition, PMOS and common-gate NMOS with opposite parasitic capacities were utilized to ensure low RMS phase error. We also optimize the size of the PMOS to achieve a wide gain control range. The core size of the designed chip was 0.056 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The designed device shows a 16.0 dB gain control range from 0 to 16.0 dB. The measured 3-dB bandwidth is 6 GHz and the measured RMS phase error is lower than 2.67°.

articleTitle: A Ka-band low noise amplifier in 0.1 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ Gallium Arsenide pHEMT process
abstract: A compact, high-gain Ka-band low noise amplifier implemented in WIN Semiconductor's 0.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathbf{m}$</tex> Gallium Arsenide process is presented in this paper. The amplifier consists of three stages with source inductive feedback at the common source of the first stage to achieve simultaneous noise and input match. The amplifier operates at 3 V drain voltage and -0.4 V gate voltage. The measured small signal gain of the amplifier is approx. 30 dB between 26 to 36 GHz, at a nominal bias, with a gain flatness of 0.65 dB. The measured average noise figure is 1.3 dB across the band for a nominal bias. The amplifier achieves a saturated output power of 16 dBm at a nominal bias and 17.5 dBm at a high bias across most of the band. The output P1dB of the amplifier is 16 dBm. The size of the amplifier is 1.1mm x 0.9 mm including the RF and DC pads.

articleTitle: A 1.5kW 90V S-band GaN Transistor for Air Traffic Control Radars
abstract: The inherent opportunity to achieving kW power level for S-band Air Traffic Control (ATC) radars with GaN transistors operated at voltages higher than industry standard of 50V is discussed. To that extent, an RF GaN/SiC transistor is reported with 1.5kW output power that operates at 90V with >10W/mm power density. Power gain is 11 dB and drain efficiency 50%. The radar signal used has 100μs pulse width and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> duty cycle. The peak power here reported is believed to be 2x higher than available in the industry at S-band, and it has been possible thanks to the 90V DC bias operation.

articleTitle: A Highly Efficient W-Band Rectifier MMIC in InP HBT Technology
abstract: This paper presents a highly-efficient on-chip W-band single-diode rectifier for energy recovery in 6G transmitters and wireless power transfer applications. For the first time a W-band rectifier has been fabricated on an InP HBT process. The circuit consists of a 2 x (0.85 x 6 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) series p-n diode as the core rectification element and a big shunted capacitor. No input matching has been applied. At 108 GHz the rectifier achieves a measured record power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 69% for - 1.5 dBm RF input power (RFin). The PCE reaches 14 % for RFin of about 15 dBm with 5 mW of DC output power. The chip shows a very compact size with 360 x 260 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads.
